dom.title: Trust & controls, Origin, the evidence layer for AI agents
dom.text:

origin

TRUST & CONTROLS

Evidence you can inspect. Limits you can see.

A useful reference check starts with a clear boundary. Origin evaluates a bound configuration against deterministic synthetic tasks and gives reviewers an artifact they can recheck.

Working prototype. Seeking design partners. Not production SaaS, compliance certification, or a guarantee of approval.

Inspect an artifact
Understand the boundary
Generated illustration of a review environment; not an Origin facility or customer deployment.
01Current posture
02Verification
03Data & retention
04Responsibility
05Security review

01 / CURRENT POSTURE

What exists today. What still needs agreement.

The public prototype demonstrates an evaluation and evidence workflow. A runtime gate and controlled tool-call proxy remain proposed pilot architecture, not deployed general enforcement.

Available now
Browser-local evaluation

Run synthetic support or IAM tasks through deterministic policy logic. Bind the configuration, inspect the verdict, and download the evidence.

Available now
Explicit artifact provenance

The public reference-check artifact is browser-session-signed and unpinned. Execution was not attempted. A valid signature does not establish trusted Origin issuance.

Proposed architecture
Controlled execution

Permission checks, a controlled proxy, named approvals, and runtime enforcement are a proposed integration path. They are not evidence of a customer deployment.

Integrity is a specific claim. “Tamper-evident” means an alteration can be detected by the relevant digest, signature, binding, or chain check. It does not establish safety, production readiness, or reviewer acceptance.

02 / VERIFICATION

The checks have a record, too.

The deterministic oracle is the sole label and reward authority. make gates-all runs the public repository's build, tests, evidence checks, and honesty checks. Inspect the CI definition or reproduce the checks locally.

2026-09-26 · ALL GATES GREEN · 14 suites — local run of make gates-all at 42934dc. CI runs its own checks on pushes to main.

✓	ts:build (chronos-ui)	✓ built in 441ms

✓	ev:reward:diff	OK — every exploit is driven to 0 and every gold is preserved (rewar
✓	ev:/verify selftest	ALL PASS — /verify detect+verify logic reproduces under Node

✓	py:chronos	411 passed, 5 skipped

A timestamped snapshot is evidence of that run, not a live assurance. Numbers in this scoreboard are reproducible under this verifier on the public repository. Private research metrics published elsewhere have separate provenance.

03 / DATA & RETENTION

Different workflows. Different data boundaries.

The public reference check, a contact request, and an authorized pilot are different activities. Their data handling should not be conflated.

WORKFLOW	DATA BOUNDARY	RETENTION POSTURE
Synthetic reference check	Browser-local policy evaluation and downloadable demo artifacts. No production action is attempted.	Public evaluation does not require submitting customer traces or credentials.
Contact request	Information you choose to provide when requesting a review. There are no customer accounts; the console is owner-only.	Contact deletion can be requested. Account and service handling are described in the privacy policy.
Foundry image processing	The public site offers a local sample. An enabled local/backend demo requires affirmative consent before an image is sent to Cerebras.	The Origin handler does not intentionally persist the image; provider terms and retention apply. See the processing disclosure.
Separately authorized pilot	Evidence, permissions, redaction, and data-use scope must be agreed before customer material is used.	Retention, deletion, and deployment-specific controls are not finalized; settle them in the pilot agreement and DPA.

04 / RESPONSIBILITY

Verification informs a decision. It does not take ownership of it.

Capability is not permission. The customer retains responsibility for its systems, agent deployment, business decisions, and release authority.

01 / Evaluation
Deterministic authority

The verifier evaluates the bound checks. Model output does not grade itself. A failed integrity or configuration check invalidates the relevant artifact.

02 / Evidence
Check the artifact type

Supported artifacts carry different bindings, signatures, digests, chains, or inclusion proofs. The verifier reports the checks and limitations of the artifact you provide.

03 / Release
A named owner decides

A demo result does not grant production access. Integration design, access controls, incident ownership, and residual risk need separate review and agreement.

05 / SECURITY REVIEW

Start with the questions your reviewer needs answered.

A founder-led review can scope a security packet for one workflow. Origin does not claim SOC 2, ISO, or any compliance certification.

ITEM	STATUS	WHAT TO CONFIRM
Data Processing Agreement	Not finalized	Data scope, permitted uses, retention, and deletion for the engagement.
Subprocessors	By request	The infrastructure and providers relevant to the proposed workflow.
Security checklist	By request	Current prototype controls and the integration work still required.
Incident ownership	Pilot-specific	Named contacts, escalation, and deployment-specific responsibilities.
Bring one workflow. Start with its boundary.
